name: Skinvive
lead: Skinvive (Juvederm Volite VYC-12) is a hyaluronic acid injectable made by Allergan that is placed in the skin itself in many small microdroplets to improve skin quality, rather than to add volume.[1][2] It belongs to the Juvederm range of hyaluronic acid products.[3]
Evidence found is limited to a 2025 split-face trial of combined botulinum toxin and Skinvive and a handful of manufacturer-linked registered trials, including one of Volite for neck lines.

paras: Hyaluronic acid is a substance found naturally in skin, and cross-linked forms in fillers last longer than natural hyaluronic acid; the body absorbs Juvederm filler usually within six to nine months.[3] Skinvive is the product name for Juvederm Volite VYC-12 in the study literature.[1]

A 2025 randomized, double-blind split-face trial in 25 women evaluated onabotulinumtoxinA combined with Juvederm Volite VYC-12 (Skinvive) for moderate and severe canthal lines, assessing efficacy, safety and durability.[1] A phase 3 trial of Juvederm Volite XC for neck lines enrolled 159 participants.[4] Other registered studies examine microdroplet hyaluronic acid on skin quality in people using GLP-1 agonists and satisfaction after jawline and neck treatment.[5][6]

For Juvederm fillers, reported effects include temporary redness, pain, swelling and bruising, and less commonly granulomas.[3] A laboratory study found that hyaluronidase can dissolve 22 commercial hyaluronic acid fillers, which is relevant to managing filler complications.[2]

card.summary: Microdroplet hyaluronic acid injected into the skin for texture and glow; early-stage evidence.
card.note: Injectable medical procedure; trial evidence is recent and small.

quick.overview:
Skinvive is an Allergan hyaluronic acid product injected into the skin to improve skin quality such as hydration and fine lines, not volume.

Published evidence is small and recent, including a 25-person split-face trial combined with botulinum toxin.
quick.mechanism: Hyaluronic acid binds water in skin; here it is placed in many tiny droplets within the skin.
quick.risks: Filler injections can cause redness, swelling, bruising and, less commonly, granulomas. It is a clinician-administered product.
